title: Snevily's conjecture for finite abelian groups of odd order
statement: Let $G$ be a multiplicatively written abelian group of odd order, and let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$ be two $k$-subsets of $G$. **Snevily's conjecture.** There is a permutation $\pi\in S_k$ such that $a_1b_{\pi(1)},\ldots,a_kb_{\pi(k)}$ are distinct. This conjecture concerns distinct representatives in products of two subsets of an abelian group; the paper notes that it is known for cyclic groups of odd order and that its validity follows from the determinant conjecture stated later for general finite abelian groups.
source_name: Tao Feng, Zhi-Wei Sun and Qing Xiang, “Exterior algebras and two conjectures on finite abelian groups”, arXiv:0808.2753 (2011).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2753

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2008).
